newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC cuts estimate for 1997 French grain sowings.
newsitem.headline: ONIC cuts estimate for 1997 French grain sowings.

text.p: France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday it had revised down its estimate for French grain sowings for the 1997 harvest.
In a document released ahead of ONIC's monthly news conference, the office said sowings were expected to rise by 3.7 percent to 6.709 million hectares over 1996.
ONIC predicted last month that sowings would grow by 3.8 percent to 6.715 million hectares. That estimate excluded spring barley, maize and sorghum.
The new estimate excludes spring barley
ONIC said soft wheat sowings may rise by 4.17 percent to 4.95 million hectares.
Winter barley sowings were seen rising by 5.5 percent to 1.12 million hectares while durum wheat sowings were lowered by 2.6 percent to 262,770 hectares.
Triticale sowings were expected to rise by 0.61 percent to 199,660 hectares.
Oats sowings were forecast down 6.43 percent to 130,900 hectares and rye sowings down 1.64 percent to 48,120 hectares.
